subject: Telemetry scope and redaction follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Becker <ab@caregridhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Telemetry scope and redaction follow-up

Alex — great call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the engineering deep-dive:

Key asks you raised during discovery:
- Which fields in request/response logs will be considered PII and need redaction (headers, cookies, body fields, trace IDs)
- Retention window expectations for audit/debug logs and backups
- Whether logs and backups must remain in EU-only storage and evidence for residency
- Access controls / SLA for audit log exports to your security team

What Redwood can offer (high-level):
- Redaction controls at ingest: configurable suppress / partial-mask / hash for headers and body fields
- Trace IDs: option to 1) drop, 2) prefix-hash (deterministic hash of trace id), or 3) full remove before storage
- Retention: per-customer retention policies (30d/90d/365d) and ability to disable long-term snapshots for Dedicated/Private installs
- Residency: EU-only storage available via Private or Dedicated deployments; hosted accounts can be region-pinned to eu-west-1 with contractual residency guarantees
- Access controls: role-based access + read-only audit exports; support for expedited export under SLA for SOC or incident response

Immediate next steps (owners & target dates):
1) Sean/Jordan: finalise redaction matrix for your list of sensitive fields and share sample scrubbed logs — target Tue, Dec 2 (attachment: redaction_matrix_v1.csv)
2) CareGrid: confirm list of fields that must be considered PII and designate privacy engineer to join the demo (we suggested Maya) — target Mon, Dec 1
3) Redwood: prepare a 30–45m sanitized-demo that shows ingest -> redaction -> retained logs and an export flow — propose week of Dec 8; draft scope attached (demo-scope-proposal.pdf)

If that looks right, can you confirm who from your side will join the demo and two preferred time windows for Dec 8–12? Also flag any non-negotiable legal/residency constraints we should bake into the demo (e.g., no backups outside EU, no deterministic hashes allowed).

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0139

Attachments: redaction_matrix_v1.csv, demo-scope-proposal.pdf

From: Alex Becker <ab@caregridhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Krishnan <maya@caregridhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 18:24:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Telemetry scope and redaction follow-up

Thanks for the clear recap, Sean. A few clarifications from our privacy team so we can finalise the field list before the demo:

- CareGrid considers any patient-identifying token and any long-lived session token as PII. That includes cookies, Authorization headers, and any user_id or email fields in request/response bodies.
- For trace IDs: we cannot retain deterministic mappings that can be reversed or correlated back to a user. A one-way hash with a salt that you control may be acceptable but we need to see the approach and threat model.
- Retention: default is 90 days; backups must not be stored outside EU boundaries for accounts serving EU patients.
- Evidence: we will need a written statement and technical proof that backups/snapshots are disabled or stored in EU only.

Can you include an example of a sanitized log line (for a simple request/response pair) ahead of the demo so our privacy team can review? Also please add our procurement lead on the follow-ups — I'll loop them in after the demo.

— Alex
Alex Becker
Director, Platform Engineering — CareGrid Health
ab@caregridhealth.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Becker <ab@caregridhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Krishnan <maya@caregridhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Telemetry scope and redaction follow-up

Alex — great, thank you. Two responses inline then next steps.

1) PII fields: we can treat cookies, Authorization headers, user_id/email fields as "sensitive" and apply an ingest pipeline rule to redact or hash them. We will send a redaction matrix with configurable action per field (redact / hash / remove). See attached masking-examples.txt for patterns we apply.

2) Trace IDs: we do not store reversible mappings by default. Options:
   - Drop trace IDs at ingest (recommended when association is not needed)
   - Prefix-hash with a per-customer salt (one-way SHA256) so you can still correlate within your account but not map back externally
   - Replace with an ephemeral UUID generated at ingest

3) Retention & backups: hosted accounts can be region-pinned to eu-west-1 and we support contractual commitments on backups. For the strongest guarantee we recommend Dedicated or Private where backups/snapshots can be administratively disabled or restricted to EU-only storage. We will provide a compliance note and a technical diagram for the residency proof.

4) Example sanitized log: uploaded a short example to Drive for your privacy team to review: https://drive.redwood/telemetry/samples/sanitized-example.log — it shows a before/after pair with Authorization header removed and trace id replaced with a hashed token.

Proposed demo slots (30–45m, hands-on):
- Tue Dec 9: 09:00–09:45 CET (00:00–00:45 PT)
- Wed Dec 10: 14:00–14:45 CET (05:00–05:45 PT)

If either works for you and Maya, we will book and prepare the canary data set (fully scrubbed) to run through the pipeline. I can also share the redaction matrix update by EOD Tue.

Jordan / Laura — can you own prepping the sanitized dataset and ensure the example demonstrates both prefix-hash and full removal?

Thanks — Sean

Attachments: masking-examples.txt

From: Alex Becker <ab@caregridhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Krishnan <maya@caregridhealth.com>, CareGrid Privacy <privacy@caregridhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 16:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Telemetry scope and redaction follow-up

Thanks — Wed Dec 10 14:00 CET works for Maya and me. Please book the invite and include the sanitized-example.log in the calendar packet.

Quick ask from our side before the demo: could you include two short examples in the Drive file — one where trace IDs are removed, and one where trace IDs are hashed with a customer-specific salt? Our privacy team wants to verify the hashing approach and confirm it meets our non-reversible requirement.

Also please include a short bullet in the demo showing how backups/snapshots are restricted to EU-only locations (a screenshot or a single-step admin toggle is fine).

I'll loop procurement after the demo. Looking forward to the walkthrough.

— Alex
